title: The Hollow Thorn
premise: Yara Thornbury, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, a smugglers' covenant that trades in memories, names, and small miracles. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Yara discovers the child is a living fragment of the broken covenant between the human realms and the Hollow — the thorned world beneath — and that the guild's founders caused the breach. Hunted by the Crown's inquisitors and betrayed by her own guildmaster, Yara must gather the scattered oaths of the old swordspeakers and reforge the covenant before the moon completes its thirteenth turn. In the end she sacrifices her own remembered past to seal the pact, choosing love for the child and justice outside the law over duty to crown or guild.
about_author: Petra Nystrom is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath-books before turning to fiction. She writes from a farmhouse on the Baltic coast, where she keeps an unreasonable number of keys and claims none of them open anything.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Miracles
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A night of routine trades at the guild: a widow buys back one hour of her husband's voice; a thief sells his name. Yara records each entry in the great ledger, establishing the guild's rules and her own rigid devotion to them. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: A Knock Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A child appears at the guild door during a storm, barefoot, unafraid, speaking a language no one recognizes — until Yara realizes her oath-blade hums in answer. The guildmaster, Corvane, orders the child turned away. Emotional beat: unease; the first crack in Yara's obedience.

chapters.title: What the Blade Remembers
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. When Yara touches the child, her sword speaks its first words in twenty years: 'Thirteenth turn.' She hides the child in the ledger vault, breaking guild law for the first time. Emotional beat: fear braided with a fierce, unfamiliar protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Wax Seal
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Dain Marrec's POV. The Crown's inquisition arrives asking after 'a vessel of the old tongue.' Marrec is courteous, patient, and utterly ruthless; he burns a memory-dealer's shop as a courtesy warning. Emotional beat: cold dread; the law as predator.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns of the Moon
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Researching forbidden ledgers, Yara learns the covenant between realms was sealed by twelve swordspeakers and shattered when the guild stole the thirteenth oath — the child itself. The moon's thirteenth turn ends the grace period. Emotional beat: horror at her guild's founding sin.

chapters.title: The Market of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Seeking the first scattered oath, Yara bargains at a black market where lifespans are currency, trading three years of her own memory. Emotional beat: the cost made flesh; she forgets her mother's face and grieves without knowing why.

chapters.title: Corvane's Kindness
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The guildmaster discovers the hidden child but, surprisingly, shields her — revealing he has known about the broken covenant for decades and fears it more than the Crown. Emotional beat: ambiguous alliance; kindness with rot beneath.

chapters.title: The Second Oath, Kept in Salt
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In a drowned chapel, Yara recovers the second oath from a swordspeaker who became coral rather than break her word. The blade drinks the salt-oath and grows heavier. Emotional beat: awe; the weight of kept promises.

chapters.title: Marrec Offers Mercy
chapters.summary: Dain Marrec's POV. Marrec corners Yara and offers a bargain: surrender the child and he will lose the guild's file forever. He genuinely believes he is saving everyone. Emotional beat: temptation; the seductive logic of lawful cruelty.

chapters.title: The Child Speaks
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Under the third oath's moonlight, the child speaks comprehensible words for the first time: her name is Vess, and she remembers being twelve people once. Emotional beat: heartbreak; personhood restored to a thing treated as cargo.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Vault
chapters.summary: Guild traitor Sef's POV. Sef sells the child's location to Marrec, believing the guild can survive only by feeding the Crown something. The vault burns; the ledgers of impossible things begin to burn with it. Emotional beat: bitter pragmatism curdling into guilt.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Thornwood
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara flees with Vess into the thorned borderland between realms, pursued by inquisitors. The thorns test them with illusions drawn from their own memories. Emotional bond deepens into chosen family. Emotional beat: terror transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Beneath the world, the Hollow's court of exiled oaths judges them. Vess is recognized as their stolen thirteenth; Yara is condemned as heir to the thieves. Emotional beat: judgment without mercy — yet a door left open.

chapters.title: An Oath Is a Debt
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. To buy time, Yara swears a swordspeaker's oath binding her life to the covenant's restoration. If she fails, the blade will take her. Emotional beat: solemnity; love formalized as sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Fourth Through Ninth
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, montage structure. A desperate season gathering six oaths from graves, rivers, and one living madwoman who kept hers too well. Each recovery costs Yara another memory. Emotional beat: mounting depletion; what remains when the self is spent?

chapters.title: Corvane Falls
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Marrec arrests the guildmaster, who dies refusing to give up Yara's route — his decades of cowardice ending in one act of courage. Emotional beat: tragic redemption; too late, but not worthless.

chapters.title: The Tenth and Eleventh
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The final two oaths lie across the sea and inside Marrec's own evidence vault. Yara chooses the impossible: break into the inquisition itself. Emotional beat: audacity born of having nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: What Marrec Keeps
chapters.summary: Dain Marrec's POV. Inside the vault, Yara finds Marrec's secret: he is himself an unbroken twelfth oath, sworn to the Crown so long ago he has forgotten he ever served the Hollow. Emotional beat: pity for the enemy; duty as a cage.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Turn
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara offers Marrec his lost oath instead of a fight. He wavers, then lets her take it — and the law he served begins to crack around him. Emotional beat: mercy as the sharpest weapon.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Night
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the moon's full thirteenth turn, with eleven oaths reforged, the covenant demands its price: a twelfth speaker must give up everything she remembers. Yara steps forward. Emotional beat: climax; love measured in total loss.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. As Yara's memories dissolve, Vess refuses to let the covenant take them all — she splits herself back into twelve souls, giving up her singular self to complete the circle. The realms knit closed. Emotional beat: mutual sacrifice; both saved, neither whole.

chapters.title: The Ledger Left Open
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, epilogue tone. Months later, Yara runs a smaller, honest trade with gaps in her past she has stopped mourning. A girl with familiar eyes brings her a book written in the old tongue. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; some debts are paid in joy.
